what_it_does: Designing analog circuits — the parts of a chip that deal with continuous real-world signals like sound or radio waves — is extremely difficult, and most AI tools that try to help start from known circuit blueprints and tweak them. EVA instead tries to invent entirely new circuit topologies from scratch, meaning it figures out which components to connect to which pins without starting from an existing template. It uses a type of large language model called a decoder-only transformer (the same architecture behind text generators) that predicts connections one step at a time, building the circuit from the bottom up. The model is first pre-trained on a large set of unlabeled circuit diagrams to learn common wiring patterns, then fine-tuned using two reinforcement-learning techniques — PPO and DPO — to push it toward designs that actually perform well.
